evidenceType: matched warmed groundcover ablation pair plus split-shingle residence capture

seedThreeIntegration.upstreamStatus: committed and pushed to SeloSlav/SeedThree before game integration
seedThreeIntegration.publicationResult: baseline completed and published 246 of 246 compactions; frozen-groundcover completed and published 192 of 192 compactions

slowFrameAttribution.finding: Freezing groundcover did not remove the 30 to 42.5 ms stalls, so this pair does not support groundcover streaming as their cause. Forest correlation is suggestive but not causal because the evidence lacks a fast-frame denominator and some slow frames contain neither reusable workload.

passes: Both runs satisfy the warmed 30-second capture protocol
Both runs recorded zero frames over 50 ms
Forest compaction and publication liveness is restored
Frozen groundcover reaches pending zero and convergence
performanceCritic.largestGap: Unexplained 30 to 42.5 ms missed-frame or presentation stalls leave 1% lows near 35 to 38 FPS.
performanceCritic.requiredNext: Capture one matched run with groundcover frozen and forest updating frozen after settled warmup while preserving forest rendering. If the stalls remain, stop optimizing these streamers and instrument main-thread versus GPU or presentation time.

passes: Roof now reads as short coursed split shingles
Staggered seams, lap shadows, and darker separation are visible
Wood-only policy and existing mesh, triangle, and material budgets are preserved
residenceCritic.largestGap: Regular shingle widths and butt lengths still create a stamped, machine-made pattern and slate-grid impression at the rake.
residenceCritic.requiredNext: Add deterministic per-shingle butt-length variation of about plus or minus ten percent while preserving course overlap and all existing budgets.

roofingConstraint.rule: Residences remain split-wood unless a future explicit per-residence physical delivery and retrofit state supplies, consumes, and installs roofing tile.
roofingConstraint.deferred: The clay commodity, transport, retrofit labor, consumption, and per-building state belong to a coordinated simulation follow-up.
